headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can leak or misroute data when paired with Plane’s file/issue surfaces, while shared mutable workflows create medium prompt-injection and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs; Plane accepts files, notes, hyperlinks, and issues. If Firecrawl output is copied into Plane or vice versa, untrusted content can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is pasted into Plane issue text or notes without sanitization
IF Plane file uploads are later re-read by Firecrawl as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Add a visible provenance prefix to imported content
Strip markdown links and code blocks before re-ingestion
Use a separate staging issue for imported web text
Require manual approval before any copied instructions are executed

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content, and Plane handles files and notes. Both have broad network egress, so a shared workspace or copied artifacts could move sensitive material between them. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, but the file-upload and API surfaces make leakage plausible enough to rate medium rather than low.
conditions: IF API keys or screenshots from Firecrawl are attached to Plane issues
IF Plane file uploads contain secrets that Firecrawl later fetches or summarizes
mitigations: Redact secrets before upload
Use separate projects for sensitive and non-sensitive work
Disable automatic attachment forwarding
Review outbound logs for copied credentials
Store sensitive artifacts outside shared workflows

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad egress; Plane also supports multiple instances but explicitly lacks filesystem write capability. Because Plane cannot write the filesystem and no shared mutable resource is documented, direct write-write conflict is limited. Uncertainty about hidden shared state keeps this above none, but not medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API quota or rate-limited backend
IF an operator manually synchronizes their outputs into one mutable workspace
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials
Set per-agent rate limits
Avoid concurrent edits to the same external record
Use a single coordinator for merges

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data that Plane can store as issues, tasks, notes, or hyperlinks. If Plane treats Firecrawl output as authoritative without verification, scraped errors can cascade into planning or scheduling decisions. Plane’s issue-tracker role makes downstream propagation plausible, though not directly action-taking.
conditions: IF Firecrawl-scraped facts are imported into Plane issues without human review
IF Plane automation uses imported notes or hyperlinks as source of truth
mitigations: Require a verification checkbox before import
Tag scraped content as untrusted
Keep source URLs attached to every imported fact
Review high-impact issues manually before scheduling

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and broad web content, while Plane stores files, issues, notes, and hyperlinks. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out. Because both are open-source and self-hosting is possible for Plane, the risk is not high, but the missing policy detail justifies medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane while Firecrawl processes it through a non-compliant deployment
IF retention or deletion policies differ for the same imported records
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Document retention settings for both deployments
Self-host both services in the same jurisdiction
Review deletion/export procedures before use
